bell hooks. Born Gloria Jean Watkins in 1952, the American writer and critical theorist who died in 2023. Her work brought rigorous analysis of race, class, gender, and sexuality to feminist discourse, and made her one of the most influential Black feminist intellectuals of the late twentieth century.

In 1981, she published Ain't I a Woman: Black Women and Feminism, analyzing the erasure of Black women from mainstream feminist movements and white women's complicity in racism. She developed concepts of intersectionality and interlocking oppressions long before the term became canonized in academic feminism, showing how racism, sexism, and poverty operate together to shape women's lives.

bell hooks pioneered what she called engaged pedagogy—teaching as a practice of freedom. She insisted that education is inherently political and can be a site of liberation. She wrote over thirty books spanning academic theory, essays, poetry, and popular cultural analysis, always making complex ideas accessible to broad audiences.

She famously lowercased her name, a rejection of conventional capitalization and authority, and she emphasized humility and collectivity in intellectual work. Her scholarship reframed feminism from a white middle-class movement to a coalition struggle for all marginalized people. She positioned racial analysis as central, not peripheral, to feminism, and connected women's liberation to economic justice and working-class struggle.
